headline: spot at a fresh three-year high, up 95% in a year, as Middle East escalation and an extended Qatari LNG force majeure lift the entire curve
commentary: UK power spot is 147.24 £/MWh, a fresh three-year high and up 94.6% on a year ago. Two things are driving it. Middle East risk: escalating US-Iran tension, including military strikes and reported attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities, is putting a premium on crude that feeds straight through to gas and power, with talks between Iran and Oman on Strait of Hormuz shipping the thing to watch. And supply: Qatar has extended its LNG force majeure and suspension of shipments through the autumn, so the replacement cargoes Europe would normally pull in simply are not available. The move runs across the whole curve, not just the front month - every gas and power contract we track rose at the latest settlement (25 of 25), and over 30 days Summer 27 gas is up 35.8% and Cal 27 up 35.2%. The longer-dated contracts a renewal actually prices against have travelled further than one day's move suggests. Curve shape still favours term. Winter 26 at 196.82 p/therm against Summer 27 at 129.30 and Winter 27 at 123.75 means a 12-month starting this October sits entirely on the expensive winter, while a 24-month blends it with a cheaper 2027/28. With the driver geopolitical and impossible to time, the question is term length, not waiting for a lower entry.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Oct 26) is 195.59 p/therm and the winter strip is higher still - Winter 26 at 196.82 and Jan 27 at 200.20. Every contract on the board rose at the latest settlement, on renewed Middle East tension and Qatar's extended LNG force majeure. Summer 27 (129.30) and Winter 27 (123.75) still sit around a third lower, so next winter remains the expensive part of the curve, but both are up roughly 36% over 30 days - the far curve is repricing too.
